AB de Villiers

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We sit down for an insight into how AB de Villiers became one of South Africa's most loved sportsmen and best batsmen in the world

Summary:
AB DE VILLIERS


AB de Villiers is one of the finest batsmen ever to play cricket, and yet his achievement extends beyond his outrageous armoury of drives, pulls, paddles, scoops and flicks.
Whether he is delighting home crowds at the Wanderers or Newlands or setting new records in Bengaluru or Sydney, he plays the game in a whole-hearted manner that projects a positive image of his country around the world and also makes millions of South Africans feel good about themselves.
This is AB’s story, in his own words … the story of the youngest of three talented, sports-mad brothers growing up in Warmbaths, of a boy who excelled at tennis, rugby and cricket, of a youngster who made his international debut at the age of 20 and was then selected in every single Test played by South Africa for the next 11 seasons, of a batsman who has started to redefine the art, being ranked among the world’s very best in Test, ODI and T20.
Through all the pyrotechnics and consistency, AB has remained a true sportsman – quick to deflect praise, swift to praise opponents, eager to work hard, to embrace the team’s next challenge and to relish what he still regards as the huge privilege of representing his country.
This is the story of a modern sporting phenomenon.


The statistics tell barely half the story but, so far, AB DE VILLIERS has scored 14 000 runs in 98 Tests for South Africa, 8 000 runs in 190 one-day internationals and more than 40 000 runs in his professional career. He is mainly distinguished by the style in which he bats and his humble, determined captaincy of the South African national team in one-day international cricket.


Further information:
AB DE Villiers
He is considered one of the best batsmen in the world. AB de Villiers reveals his early years in Warmbaths at 20 Mentz avenue, how as the youngest of 3 brothers, his cricket career was shaped. AB came from a sports mad family and his garden became an imaginary sports park, his brothers and himself became their sporting heroes.

AB was destined for a career in tennis but it was team sports that attracted him and so after years as a potentially great tennis player he concentrated on cricket and rugby. From his first selection into the F team at AFFIES he eventually made it into the first team.

He speaks of how he learnt early habits of discipline at the hands of his mentors and the importance of having someone believe in you.

He reveals school boy antics – like his pirate radio station beaming school boy naughtiness into the girls high that got him expelled from boarding school ….

He tells of the incredible game at the Wanderers in 2015 against the West Indies were record after record was broken but how before he goes out to bat he is wracked with nerves. He also reveals that he is not mad about being in the limelight.

This all round sportsman reveals his love for his high school AFFIES that was the foundation of his cricket career. How a trunk of precious memorabilia of his days there is secretly buried somewhere on the sportsfield- only to be dug up in 2022.

We tell the story of one of South Africa’s most remarkable and loved sportsmen.

AB de Villiers
He was only twenty years old when he played his debut match against England in late 2004. Since then there’s been no stopping South African cricketer Abraham Benjamin de Villiers or "AB" as he is called by fans across the globe. Carte Blanche gets up close and personal with a star who is widely regarded as the best batsman in the world.


Script:


AB De Villiers FINAL SCRIPT TX Sunday 4th September 2016

Commentary One
It all began on their lawn in Warmbaths – Ab De Villiers and his two older brothers imagining they were cricket legends battling it out on the international stage. They called the lawn DIV PARK

AB
I think I grew up on that lawn – brothers shunting me around and before I knew it there was a cricket pitch on DIV Park

Commentary Two
But sometimes Young Ab’s dreams were crushed, as the little kid, wearing a cap from his hero Jonty Rhodes, competed against his bigger brothers and their friend Gerhard

AB
Gerhard Deist was bowling -I dropped the catch and he asked me to take the cap off, that I was not worthy of wearing the cap, so it was a huge moment I will never forget it, that made me want to prove a point to him and all the other older guys including my brothers

Commentary Three
Its these and other moments that AB DE VILLIERS, currently one of the worlds best batsman, reveals in his new book. But he says he is just a simple guy.

ABE
I love my wife, my family and I love cricket.

Commentary Four
He recalls his five years at Afrikaans hoer Seuns School as some of the best of his life

ABE
The minute I walked into that school I felt part of something bigger than just the individual.

Commentary Five
AB excelled at all sport, but team sports held a special attraction for him and so he gave up a potential tennis career for cricket

Bongani
If one looks at your career from the time you finish high school, as an outsider it looks like it was part of a grand plan, a fairy tale even, but you say it didn’t happen quite that precisely

ABE
I knew where I was going and I could hear the crowds cheering, but I very often found myself having a pepper steak pie in Hatfield with too many beers and then playing a cricket game the next day and thinking this is not how we will end up playing for the Proteas but its ok we are still going

Commentary Six
But the boy with talent was soon noticed.

Up sound match
Abe de Villiers he will be very nervous, its his debut

Commentary Seven
By the time he was 20, he was opening the batting against England and fielding at point

Up sound
Well taken by Abe De Villiers

ABE
It wasn’t that good, not even remotely as good as the catch I took in the swimming pool growing up with my brothers. Before I knew it I had a reputation of being a good fielder
and maybe the next Jonty Rhodes

Commentary eight
Three months later the shy boy from Bela Bela would soon come face to face with cricket legend Brian Lara at a function in Trinidad

ABE
I was never going to introduce myself to him so I hung around Boucher my comfort zone. Out of nowhere I was ordering a beer, Boucher left… so in this first test match they couldn’t pronounce my name ABDEV and everyone started laughing .. Brian Lara approached me that night and said young man I know your name its AB D E V I L L I E R S and boy can you play cricket. WOW!

Bongani
What does it feel like when one of the greatest players of the modern era says that to you?
ABE
I scored 100s just after that! Obviously!

LINK
The conventional thinking around talent and hard work has always been that anyone can achieve something but talent is the magic ingredient that makes someone special. ABE flips that around and says the talent was always there but it was the hard work that took him from good to great

AB
so talent yes it opened up doors for me but they don’t score you hundreds, and they don’t win you cricket games – its that deep inner fight and the belief that opened the real doors

Up sound
He is right in front and he has got him



Commentary nine
And he soon needed that inner fight because a year after his debut, failure loomed and here at SuperSport Park he found his dream disappearing

ABE
between 20 and 25 I was lost and completely nowhere – the boy with the talent. I had to say listen who do you want to be where do you want to play your cricket and who do you want to be remembered as? As the boy who can hit a couple of fours or the guy who is remembered as the one who is always there at the end when the team needs him

Commentary ten
Today, his achievements extend beyond his repetoire of drives, pulls, hooks, sweeps and flicks– he has scored more than 8000 runs in Test cricket and One day internationals with an incredible average of over 50. He has also the SA test side

Bongani
Do you have any appreciation of the kind of magic you ignite around the world in would be cricketers?
AB
Its really difficult for me to make peace with that and understand that, I remember those moments seeing Jonty in the nets and yes I am shy and humble but you have to put yourself out there and act like a great in front of them

Up sound

Commentary eleven
And no where is that required more than in India – a country he loves and where his name is chanted across stadia.

ABD! ABD!

Bongani
You talk about this guy from Bela bela but what is it like to be in India and need body guards?

AB De Villiers
Ya its really nice to have 50 000 people chanting your name when you walk out to bat –you feel like hero, but also that privacy problem that you go to your hotel room and you don’t have a hole to climb into

LINK WORLD CUP
Its been 24 years since SA readmission into international cricket and in that time we have produced terrific teams with some legendary names but for all their achievements one thing remains elusive, the holy grail of cricket, lifting the world cup.


AB
I started dreaming about the WC. I can see it ……its meant to be

Commentary twelve
But three times since then our world cup dreams have been dashed

AB
No one wants to be a choker. I know I am not a choker I know I can play the big moments, but unfortunately in those world cup games when we needed to do it we just haven’t done it before and haven’t done it yet because I still believe its coming

Up sound

Commentary thirteen
But the 18th January 2015 was a perfect summers day at the Wanderers

AB
You sometimes get a feeling, and that day I was very uncomfortable, stumbling out to bat, long story short the first ball goes for 4

Commentary fourteen
He needn’t have worried, as AB was about to break two world records that day- the fastest 50 and the fastest century in a One Day International

ABE
and boom it’s a blur!

Up sound

ABE
I remember Chris Gale coming up to me doing something like this and I was just in awe of what just happened

Up Sound Match

ABE
and then just before I crossed the boundary rope I remembered my parents were there …my dad never saw all my games he was a doctor missed rugby matches …but he was there and it just felt like my life was ok

THE END 8 02









PROMO ONE 10 seconds

Voice over
AB De Villiers hasn’t given up hope of winning the world cup in 2019
AB
I can see it in my dreams stopping the ball at cover point.


PROMO TWO 15 seconds
AB De Villiers – recalls some of his best cricketing moments

AB
and boom it’s a blur!

Up sound match

AB
I remember Chris Gale coming up to me doing something like that!


PROMO THREE
AB
Looking to my right Brian Lara was standing there

Voice over
Cricket Legend, Brian Lara once gave a shy boy from Bela Bela a real confidence boost.

AB
Brian Lara approached me that night and said boy you can play. Wow!
